title: ✨ IMPROVE DANCE STABILITY🏋🏻‍♀️ Lower Body Workout for Beginners + Learn Viral Kpop Footwork

method.teacher_system: The teacher breaks down complex K-pop footwork into simple, repetitive fitness-based drills. She focuses on core stability, weight shifting, and muscle engagement to build a foundation for dance. Each drill is practiced in a loop to ensure the learner masters the movement before moving to the next level.
method.signature: She uses a split-screen format that shows a professional K-pop performance on the left and her own simplified, instructional version on the right, allowing learners to see the direct application of the drill.

practices.what: The teacher breaks down the squat movement, emphasizing keeping the hips level and not letting the knees pass the toes.
The teacher leads the learner through multiple repetitions of the squat, focusing on engaging the abs, thighs, and glutes.
The teacher adds a side-to-side weight shift to the squat, instructing the learner to keep the hips level while shifting.
The teacher repeats the side-to-side weight shift, encouraging the learner to lift the leg while maintaining control.
The teacher combines the squat and the side-to-side weight shift into a single, fluid movement.
The teacher introduces a heel-pop drill, focusing on keeping the hips still while moving the feet.
The teacher increases the speed of the footwork drill, challenging the learner to maintain control at a faster tempo.
The teacher adds a heel twist to the footwork, emphasizing hip and knee control.
The teacher incorporates both legs into the footwork, focusing on weight shifting and knee angles.
The teacher adds a walking movement to the footwork, requiring the learner to maintain stability while moving.
The teacher introduces a 'knees-out' and 'knees-in' drill, using the toes to twist the heels.
The teacher adds a leg lift to the 'knees-out' and 'knees-in' drill, focusing on weight shifting.

adaptations.difficulty: Squatting too deep can cause knee strain for beginners.
adaptations.adjustment: The teacher advises beginners not to squat too much and to ensure their knees do not pass their toes.

adaptations.difficulty: The leg lift drill can cause the learner to lose balance.
adaptations.adjustment: The teacher reassures the learner that it is okay to go up and down a little bit during the movement.

feelings.response: The teacher acknowledges the difficulty and encourages the learner to keep going.
The teacher gives the learner permission to take a break, drink some water, and rest before the next part.

The teacher gives specific instructions on how to squat correctly to avoid knee pain and engage the right muscles.
The teacher confirms that the learner should be able to lift their leg if they have mastered the weight shift.

mentor.what_stays: The teacher leaves the learner feeling capable of mastering complex-looking dance moves through focused, step-by-step training.
